summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia s/p allogeneic cord blood transplant and chronic graft-versus-host disease, was admitted for acute on chronic renal failure and hyperkalemia. He experienced a brief syncopal episode upon arrival, prompting a code blue due to severe hyperkalemia, which was treated with insulin, dextrose, and kayexalate. His potassium normalized, and renal function returned to baseline. The syncopal episodes, both recent and historical, were evaluated with neurology input, leading to outpatient EEG, Holter monitor, carotid ultrasound, and echocardiogram referrals. Lisinopril was held due to hyperkalemia, Cellcept was dose-reduced, and Protonix was started for refractory gastritis. He remained stable without further events and was discharged home in good condition with follow-up arranged.
problems: Acute myeloid leukemia, without mention of having achieved remission
